mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) above 5% growth signals robust demand, which lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of elevated inflation or financial stress.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% triggers a loss of consumer confidence, reducing consumption and corporate investment, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite UNRATE falling below 4.0% within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) below 1.5% and sustained GDP growth (GDPC1) above 6% creates a dual signal of monetary easing and robust demand, amplifying equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when FEDFUNDS are below 1.5% but GDPC1 growth is weak or negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) and accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 1.75%), reduced risk premiums and increased investor confidence drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to outperform baseline in regimes with high inflation or tight monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently high monthly employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth is below 5% in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 triggers supply-side contraction, reducing corporate output and investment, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite INDPRO recovering to baseline levels within the same period.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing boom regime (HOUST > 2000), rising home construction activity signals sustained demand for equities, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to rise above baseline during periods of elevated interest rates or economic uncertainty.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 98.0 and 1.8%, respectively, create a supply-demand balance that stabilizes equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when either INDPRO or CPIAUCSL exceeds their respective thresholds.
